parole.significato: forms the plurals of some nouns of Latin origin with a singular in -us.
parole.testo: From Latin -ī (nominative plural suffix of the o-declension), in part directly, in part through Italian -i.

From New Latin, from Latin bīlis (“bile”) + Italian verde (“green”) + -in. The German word was naturalized into other languages as international scientific vocabulary (e.g., biliverdin, biliverdine, biliwerdyna).

parole.significato: lip balm; chapstick (a plastic stick including a substance that is applied to the lips to relieve dry lips)
parole.testo: From the brand name Labello, apparently a portmanteau word of Latin labium (“lip”) + bellus (“beautiful”), or similar forms in Romance languages such as Italian labbro + bello.

parole.significato: by, by means of, through, via
parole.testo: From Late Middle High German per (15th c.), from Latin per, in part through Italian per.
Ca. 1500, from Latin rata, perhaps through Italian rata and/or Middle French rate.

parole.significato: talar (ankle-length robe worn by judges or priests)
A third; an interval of 3 (minor third) or 4 (major third) semitones.
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle High German tërzje, tërze, from Latin tertia. Doublet of Tertia. The musical sense was a later semantic loan from Italian terza.
